# Rising cheese snack producer hires new CEO

The-Farmer-Companies-CEO-Randy_Johnson.jpg

Photo: The Farmer Cos.

07\.31.2026

By Zachary Sosland

[Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=foodbusinessnews.net&location=article_header)

BURLINGTON, VT. — The Farmer Cos. has named Randy Johnson as its latest chief executive officer. He will succeed the company’s founder Adam Farmer, who will transition to the role of chairman.

Johnson joins The Farmer Cos. from Dot’s Pretzels, helping raise its annual sales from $19 million to $250 million in three years and just before it was acquired by The Hershey Co. in 2021, The Farmer Companies said.

“Under Randy's leadership, Dot's Pretzels became one of the greatest success stories in snacking history. Randy set Dot's up for a strategic next step, and led the company through its transformational growth phase,” Farmer said.

# Whisps parent co. taps former Dot's Pretzels exec as CEO

## Randy Johnson will succeed founder Adam Farmer in the role.

By SF&WB Staff

Whisps parent co. taps former Dot's Pretzels exec as CEO

Courtesy of The Farmer Companies

July 31, 2026

[The Farmer Companies](https://www.thefarmercompanies.com/) announced the appointment of Randy Johnson as chief executive officer, succeeding founder Adam Farmer, who will remain active as chairman. Johnson joins the company following this month’s closing of a $17 million Series A financing led by Raff Ventures, alongside Ajax Capital Partners, as The Farmer Companies accelerates its strategy to build its North American cheese snacking business through its ownership of Whisps and exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery.

Johnson previously led [Dot’s Pretzels](https://www.hersheyland.
com/dots-pretzels) , growing the company from $19 million to $250 million in annual sales in just three years prior to its 2021 acquisition by Hershey for $1.2 billion.

“Under Randy’s leadership, Dot’s Pretzels became one of the greatest success stories in snacking history. Randy set Dot’s up for a strategic next step, and led the company through its transformational growth phase,” says Farmer. “Bringing him on means The Farmer Companies can build toward our goal of redefining cheese snacking for the next generation. Our business model is clear; we make the highest-quality cheese snacks with the best cheeses in the world. Randy is leading our business to new heights.”

The Farmer Companies’ premium cheese snacking portfolio includes Whisps, the 100% cheese crisp brand, and an exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery to produce Cabot Creamery Popcorn.

# The Farmer Companies Appoints Randy Johnson as New CEO

The former Dot's Pretzels leader joins after a $17M Series A to scale its cheese snack brands.

7/31/2026

• Ali Abounasr El Alaoui

Back to News

The Farmer Companies has appointed Randy Johnson as its new Chief Executive Officer, a strategic move following a successful $17 million Series A funding round. Johnson, renowned for his transformative leadership at Dot's Pretzels, succeeds founder Adam Farmer, who will transition to Chairman. This leadership change and capital infusion are set to accelerate the company's ambition to dominate North America's premium cheese snacking market.

* * *

## A New Era of Leadership

Randy Johnson brings a formidable track record, having previously guided Dot's Pretzels through a period of explosive growth.
Under his direction, the brand's annual sales surged from $19 million to $250 million in just three years. This impressive trajectory culminated in the company's $1.2 billion acquisition by Hershey® in 2021.

Adam Farmer expressed confidence in the appointment, highlighting Johnson's proven ability to scale brands for strategic success. Farmer stated that Johnson's leadership was instrumental in making Dot's Pretzels a historic success story. This move allows The Farmer Companies to aggressively pursue its goal of redefining the cheese snacking category for a new generation.

## Strategic Funding for Expansion

The executive transition coincides with the closing of a $17 million Series A financing round, providing significant capital for growth. The investment was led by Raff Ventures, with participation from AJAX Capital Partners. These funds are earmarked to fuel the company's strategic expansion plans across multiple business areas.
Proceeds from the financing will be deployed to enhance manufacturing partnerships and expand national distribution networks. The company also plans to pursue strategic acquisitions to further bolster its market position and product portfolio. This investment underscores investor confidence in The Farmer Companies' vision to build a leading cheese snacking enterprise.

## A Portfolio of Premium Brands

The Farmer Companies' strategy is anchored in a portfolio of high-quality, cheese-centric snack brands. This includes the iconic WHISPS®, a popular 100% cheese crisp brand acquired by the company. The portfolio is strengthened by an exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery® to produce its rapidly growing popcorn line.

Both WHISPS and Cabot Creamery Popcorn are built on a foundation of using award-winning cheese and premium ingredients. The Cabot Creamery Popcorn has already distinguished itself as the fastest-growing brand among top U.S. popcorns.
This commitment to quality is central to the company's brand identity and market appeal.

## Vision for the Future

With new leadership and fresh capital, The Farmer Companies is poised to execute its ambitious business model. Farmer noted that Johnson's appointment allows him to focus on his strengths in identifying great brands and creating unforgettable flavors. This synergy between the founder and new CEO is expected to drive innovation and market penetration.

Johnson shared his enthusiasm for the opportunity, stating his goal is to help build one of North America's great consumer products companies. He acknowledged that Farmer has already demonstrated the significant growth potential within the premium cheese snacking category. Johnson's primary role will be to scale existing operations and capitalize on emerging market opportunities.

* * *

The appointment of Randy Johnson as CEO and the successful $17 million funding round mark a pivotal moment for The Farmer Companies.
This combination of proven leadership and substantial financial backing provides a powerful catalyst for growth. The company is now exceptionally well-positioned to realize its vision of becoming the leader in the North American premium cheese snacking industry.
